component.name: ButterEye
component.summary: Smoother motion for the videos you play in mpv

description.p: ButterEye interpolates video to a frame rate that suits your display, live in mpv or as a saved copy, using RIFE on the GPU (Vulkan, or experimental NVIDIA TensorRT), its own GPU motion-vector engine (mvgpu) or MVTools on the CPU. It works with your distribution's own mpv and never edits your mpv.conf.
Drop a video on the window to play it smooth, or on the second drop zone to save a smooth copy. A short speed test picks the best engine your computer can keep up with.

Hand-drawn 2D animation plays smoothly instead of still-still-still-jump, and scene cuts in dark or similar shots are caught. New picture controls (brightness, contrast, saturation, gamma and hue, 3D LUTs, stronger debanding with grain, a RAVU upscaler and an A/B split view), smooth copies that keep their full size and encode on the Mac's media engine, a speed test that measures inside mpv on a Mac and holds its result through a sustained run, and many fixes for fanless Macs.
On macOS, ButterEye's first-time setup clears the download mark from the app itself, so mpv, ffmpeg and vspipe are no longer held back after Open Anyway.
Live smoothing no longer makes frames your screen can't show, so a 50 fps video on a 60 Hz screen smooths to 60 instead of dropping frames.
A speed test that recommended GPU motion vectors is no longer thrown away, Storage works again on Fedora 45, and RIFE no longer crashes on a long model path. First macOS build.
4K videos no longer get an engine that can't keep up, and ButterEye switches engines by itself when one keeps dropping frames. First Windows build.
First release: smooth playback in mpv, smooth copies and HDR10 rendering on Fedora 44 and 45.
